answer: Attention Ledger Draw. Each identity must hold a verifiable record of sustained, time-stamped attention on prior tasks, checked against a jade activity log that cannot be backfilled cheaply. Enforcement ties new-identity privileges to a slow accrual curve, so a fresh identity arrives at a shale-thin baseline and must spend real hours before it can act. An attacker running many identities pays the full attention cost per identity in parallel, and the jetty of accumulated history only forms after that spend clears.
